contexts.text: Only those Mohammedans are elevated into their higher Heaven who renounce concubines...
In their lower Heaven they live with a number of wives and concubines as in the world.
Polygamous love is the love of the sex, because... it is allowed to take concubines in addition to wives; and thus... is the love of lasciviousness.
The concubines and wives of polygamists are, after death, for the most part set free...
That there is also a jealousy in regard to concubines... Explained.
Jealousy in regard to concubines springs from the externals...
An invitation to love by a concubine does not so (chill the whole man). Explained.
They make one evil out of all evils, and mix them together... In like manner do they with the love of the sex, with fornication, with pellicacy, with adultery...

That with those who... cannot as yet enter into marriage, and on account of salacity cannot restrain their lusts, the Conjugial may be conserved, if the love of the sex be restricted to one mistress. Explained. SE 6054.
There seems to be no other refuge and as it were asylum, than the ascription of a mistress, who in French is called maitresse.

It is better that (the springing fountain of manhood) be reserved for a wife; but if on account of the unbridled force of lust it cannot, an intermediate method is needed, by which conjugial love may in the meantime be prevented from perishing. That this is pellicacy, is favoured by these things. (Six reasons stated.)
In pellicacy, which is a more ordinate and sane fornication, he can learn and see (these) distinctions.

By pellicacy, also, no access is given to the four kinds of lusts which are in the highest degree destructive of conjugial love... But these things are not said to those who can restrain the heat of lust; nor to those who can enter into marriage as soon as they arrive at manhood...

That pellicacy is better than wandering lust, provided it is not engaged in with more than one, nor with a virgin or unimpaired woman, nor with a married woman, and it is kept separate from conjugial love. Explained.
The reason pellicacy is not to be engaged in with more than one, is that with more than one there is what is polygamous within, which induces on man a merely natural state...

Therefore, he who adjoins to himself a virgin as a mistress, can indeed cohabit with her, and thus initiate her into the friendship of love; but still with the constant intention, if she does not commit adultery, that she be or become his wife.
That pellicacy is not to be engaged in with a married woman, because this is adultery, is evident.

The reason why the love of pellicacy is to be kept separate from conjugial love, is that these loves are distinct, and therefore are not to be commingled. For the love of pellicacy is a love unchaste, natural, and external, whereas the love of marriage is chaste, spiritual, and internal. The love of pellicacy makes distinct the souls of two persons, and conjoins only the sensuous things of the body; whereas the love of marriage unites their souls...

The love of pellicacy enters only into the understanding, and into the things which depend on the understanding; whereas the love of marriage enters also into the will... and therefore if the love of pellicacy becomes the love of marriage, the man cannot recede from any right, without a violation of the conjugial union; and if he does recede, and marries another, conjugial love perishes in the breach of it. It is to be known that the love of pellicacy is kept separate from conjugial love, by his not promising marriage to the mistress, and by his not leading her into any hope of marriage. Yet it is better that the torch of the love of the sex be first kindled with a wife.

In the preceding chapter... by pellicacy was meant the conjunction of an unmarried man with a woman under a compact... Those who do not distinguish genera, use the words (pellicacy and concubinage) promiscuously... But, as they are two genera, and the word pellicacy is suitable to the former, because a mistress is an adulteress... therefore, for the sake of separation, an ante-nuptial compact with a woman is signified by pellicacy...
